lawyer:
Md. Ashadullah Advocate ----- For the Petitioner (in both the revisions). 
Md. Anwar Hossain Advocate ----- For the Opposite-Parties (in both the revisions).
parties:
Kazi Harun Mia ----- Plaintiff-Petitioner
Vs.
Kazi Abdul Mannan ----- Defendant-Opposite-Party
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Hafiz J: The aforesaid two revisions have been arisen out of the same judgment and decree and the Rules were issued and subsequently heard analogously, thus both the Rules are to be disposed of by one judgment.

2. Both the Rules were issued calling upon the opposite party Kazi Abdul Mannan to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 19-4-2012 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Comilla in Title Appeal No. 109 of 2010 heard analogous with Title Appeal No. 110 of 2010 and thereby affirming those dated 29-4-2010 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Comilla in decreeing the Title Suit No. 44 of 2001 heard analogous with Title Suit No. 22 of 2001 should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

3. The plaintiff's Case (Title Suit No. 44 of 2001) in short is that Arfan Bibi and Ashab Uddin Kazi jointly got settlement of 60 decimals of land in dispute from the ex-landlord. Arfan Bibi died leaving behind only daughter Bodrun Nessa who sold 31 decimals land to Kazi Esmail by a registered deed No.47 dated 22-6-1944. SA Khatian No. 149 was finally published in equal shares in the name of Kazi Esmail and Kazi Mannan. Kazi Esmail gifted 29 decimals land to the petitioner Kazi Harun Mia, who is his grandson, by a registered deed of Gift dated 14-2-1960 including 4 decimals land of Plot No. 783 and he is in possession of the said land and since then the defendant Kazi Abdul Mannan threatened him and thus he (Kazi Harun) filed the instant suit for permanent injunction.

4. The opposite parties Kazi Abdul Mannan and others as plaintiff's filed Title Suit No. 22 of 2001 against Kazi Harun Mia in the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Comilla for partition of the suit land and the plaintiffs case, in short, is that Ashraf Uddin Kazi and Arfan Bibi by a registered Patta of 1314 BS got settlement of the land and by amicable partition Ashraf Uddin Kazi got 34 decimals land and Arfan Bibi got rest 25 decimals land. After the death of Ashraf Uddin Kazi his brother Bosiruddin Kazi inherited his properties and Arfan Bibi sold 25 decimals land to Bosiruddin Kazi by an unregistered deed of 1317 BS at a price of Taka 40 and as a result Bosiruddin Kazi became owner of the said land. Bosiruddin Kazi died leaving behind the said Kazi Abdul Mannan and two daughters and by amicable partition Bosiruddin Kazi got aforesaid 46.5 decimals land and he made a Waqf in favour of Mosque of an area of 30 decimals land by a deed dated 2-9-1952 and thereafter he exchanged the said land with the Mosque Committee by a Exchange deed No.4593 dated 20-11-1981 and filed the instant suit praying for decree of partition impleading Kazi Harun Mia as defendant No.1.

5. In both the suits, parties filed written statement denying the materials allegations made in the plaint. The trial Court on consideration of the records framed separate issues in both the two suits. From the record it appears that the issues in Title Suit No. 44 of 2001 and Title Suit No. 22 of 2001 were framed at the time of passing of the judgment and on that issues judgment was passed by the trial Court and no separate evidence was recorded by the trial Court in both the suits; only evidence was recorded in Title Suit No. 22 of 2001 and decreed the same (Title Suit No.22 of 2001) and dismissed the Title Suit No. 44 of 2001 by the same judgment on 29-4-2010.

6. As against the aforesaid judgment and decree the petitioner as appellant filed two separate appeals being Title Appeal No. 109 of 2010 and Title Appeal No. 110 of 2010 in the Court of District Judge, Comilla and on transfer the said two appeals were heard analogously by the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Comilla and by a common judgment dated 19-4-2012 dismissed the said two appeals and thus the petitioner moved the aforesaid two applications before this Court and obtained the Rules.

7. The petitioner filed Supplementary Affidavits and the opposite party filed Counter Affidavit in the aforesaid Revisions.

8. Mr Ashadullah, learned Advocate for the petitioner by referring "cause of action" and "reliefs prayed" from the plaint of the two title suits submits that the cause of action and the relief prayed for in both the suits disclose that the suits as a whole being different in nature and character and thus analogous judgment and recording of evidence in one suit is contrary to law. The learned Advocate then submits that the petitioner being plaintiff of Title Suit No.44 of 2001 was not allowed to adduce evidence to prove his case as defendant which is against the mandate of Order 18 of the Code of Civil Procedure and principle of natural justice. In support of his contention he has referred to the case of Abdul Latif Chowdhury vs Md Nur Hossain reported in 17 BLD (AD) 230 and emphasized on the following portion of the judgment:

"6. It is however desirable that evidence should be taken separately in respect of five different suits and cases and judgment should also be pronounced separately taking into consideration the evidence adduced in each particular suit and case. Evidence in one suit or case shall not be taken as evidence in the other suits or cases."

9. And the learned Advocate further submits that the trial Court passed the impugned judgment and decree by framing fresh issues at the time of writing of the impugned judgment and decree which is against the provisions of Order XIV, rule I of the Code of Civil Procedure as the issues are to be framed before taking evidence after considering the plaint and the written statement and the evidence is to be adduced as per issues framed and as such framing of issues at the time of passing judgment without notice to the parties is illegal and violative of principle of natural justice and in support of his contention he has referred to the case of Md Abdul Jalil Mia vs Nirupuma Ritchil reported in 17 BLD (AD) 63 = 49 DLR (AD) 61 and the relevant portion of the judgment as referred quoted as under:

"8. Order XIV rule I of the Code of Civil Procedure casts a definite responsibilities upon the trial Court to frame issue upon the material assertions by one party and denied by the other and this can be done at any stage of the suit if found necessary provided that the parties are afforded a chance to contest the issue."

10. And the learned Advocate for the petitioner by referring judgment reported in AIR 1994 Allahabad 81 and the judgment of the Appellate Division reported in 8 BLC (AD) 167 submits that the petitioner as plaintiff filed suit for permanent injunction and the opposite parties filed partition suit and both the suits are different kind of suits and there cannot be the same issue in the said suits and as such hearing of the two suits analogously are not permissible in law but simultaneous hearing is permitted by law.

11. On the other hand Mr Md Anwar Hossain, learned Advocate for the opposite parties submits that on prayer of the petitioner both the suits were heard analogously and as such he cannot raise that the hearing of the suits analogously is not permissible in law. The learned Advocate further submits that the Court has the inherent power to pass an order for analogous hearing and the petitioner did not raise objection against analogous hearing and framing of issues. Thus, at this stage the petitioner cannot raise objection against analogous hearing and framing issues. He further submits that the parties are same and both the suit land is same and thus there is no bar for analogous hearing of the suits. In support of his contentions he has referred to the cases reported in 51 DLR 352, 50 DLR 441, 30 DLR (SC) 74, 40 DLR 56, AIR 1984 (Orissa) 209, 9 BLT (AD) 148 and 66 DLR (AD) 37.

12. On the other hand Mr Asadullah submits that the consent of the parties to commit illegalities by the Court of law confers no jurisdiction upon a Court of law and the Court of law must act according to law and otherwise it will lead to chaos and anarchy and the cases referred by the learned Advocate for the opposite parties are distinguishable from the facts and circumstances of instant case and thus those are not applicable in the instant case.

13. Heard the learned Advocates for both the sides and perused the record.

<u>14. Admittedly, petitioner Kazi Harun Mia as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 58 of 2001 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Comilla for permanent injunction against the defendant-opposite party Kazi Abdul Mannan which was eventually transferred to the Court of learned Joint District Judge, Comilla renumbered as Title Suit No. 44 of 2001 and other suit i.e. Title Suit No. 22 of 2001 was filed for partion by Kazi Abdul Mannan and others as plaintiffs against the said Kazi Harun Mia as defendant. The "cause of action" and "the relief prayed for" in both the suits are different which indicates that the suits as a whole being different in nature and character and thus the petitioner as plaintiff of the Title Suit No. 44 of 2001 was not allowed to adduce evidence to prove his case as defendant of Title Suit No. 22 of 2001 which was used in passing the judgment and decree in both the suits by an analogous judgment and this is contrary to law and thus the judgment referred by the petitioner reported in 17 BLD (AD) 230 is the appropriate judgment in the instant case. The opposite party failed to show any judgment contrary to the aforesaid judgment. The judgments as referred by the opposite party are not relevant as the facts and circumstances of the cases are quite distinguishable. Considering the facts and circumstances of the aforesaid cases, analogous hearing of the aforesaid suits are not permissible in law. Moreso, the trial Court passed the impugned judgment and decree by framing fresh issues at the time of passing the judgment and decree which is also contrary to law as the issues are to be framed before taking evidence after considering the plaint and then evidence is to be adduced as per issues. I find substance in the aforesaid Rules.</u>

15. In the result, both the Rules are made absolute.

16. The impugned judgment and decree dated 19-4-2012 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Comilla in Title Appeal No. 109 of 2010 heard analogous with Title Appeal No. 110 of 2010 are hereby set-aside. Therefore, I am sending those back on remand for simultaneous hearing to the appellate Court below and to take evidence separately in respect of the two suits after framing issues separately and judgment should be pronounced separately taking into consideration the evidences adduced in each particular suit at the earliest possible time.

The lower Court record be sent down to the appellate Court below with the observations made above.

End.
